title: Audit Forwarder: Hybrid Forward Protocol + Consumable Manifest for Customer-Managed Storage
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Design and implement a hybrid audit forwarding protocol and a consumable manifest format to support customer-managed storage targets (S3/GCS/Azure and on-prem blob stores) for Private/VPC deployments. The hybrid forwarder will support both push and pull modes, explicit ack windows, resumable multipart handoff, and an attachable CMEK handshake for customer-managed keys. The intent is to provide deterministic delivery guarantees, efficient on-network resource usage (reduce sustained memory/KV cache pressure), and operator controls for retention/rotation without requiring Redwood to hold plaintext audit payloads.

Background: Current private audit forwarding prototypes rely on single-mode push flows with opaque uploads or long-lived streaming connections. Customers with strict controls want: (1) the ability to point Redwood to a customer-owned sink without exposing raw keys to the platform, (2) predictable resource usage in constrained network environments, and (3) resumable, verifiable uploads that can survive mid-file restarts and key rotations. This ticket builds the protocol and server-side runtime adapters to satisfy these needs and integrates with our existing audit-shipper architecture.

Goals:
- Define a compact, versioned manifest schema describing batches, checksums, encryption metadata, and multipart parts metadata suitable for both cloud and on-prem sinks.
- Add a hybrid forward protocol where a customer operator can choose: push (Redwood uploads directly to customer sink after an ephemeral CMEK handshake), pull (customer-operated agent polls a signed manifest and pulls parts), or a delegated transfer (Redwood issues pre-signed multipart URLs that the customer's agent finalizes).
- Implement a backpressure and windowing model: limit in-flight batches per-tenant, provide an ack/heartbeat exchange, and allow configurable retry/backoff policies.
- Support CMEK handshake flow for customer-managed keys without Redwood storing keys: sealed envelope exchange, optional HSM/KMS handshake recording, and key-rotation marker support in the manifest.
- Ensure telemetry and observability: per-tenant delivery latency, retry counts, upload success rate, and manifest verification failures.

Non-goals: Porting every legacy forwarder verbatim; full ML-assisted anomaly detection for manifests (future ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish a versioned manifest JSON schema (schema URL in links) with fields: batch_id, sequence_range, part_list (with offsets and sha256 checksums), encryption {mode, key_id_marker}, upload_strategy, and created_at.
Implement server-side endpoint /audit/forward/manifest that returns signed manifests for pull and delegated flows; signatures must be verifiable with Redwood public key.

Implement push path that performs resumable multipart uploads to S3-compatible targets with retry idempotency and exposes a CMEK handshake using envelope encryption; no customer plaintext keys are persisted in Redwood storage.

Backpressure: enforce per-tenant inflight limit (configurable, default 4 batches) and expose metrics and a visible throttle header in responses. Load tests should demonstrate stable memory < 1.2GB for 1000 rps of small audit events with 4 tenants.
Integrations test matrix: cloud S3 (AWS), GCS, Azure Blob, and a reference on-prem minio/rsync consumer agent. Each integration must complete upload and manifest verification in an end-to-end CI job.
Security review signoff recorded in Confluence and a threat model doc attached in links.
Migration plan documented and validated with 2 pilot customers on Dedicated and Private clusters without data loss during a key rotation exercise.
implementation_notes: Protocol design doc: draft at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Hybrid+Audit+Forward+Protocol (see v0.1 manifest spec)
Manifest schema stored as JSON Schema in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/blob/main/manifest-schema/v1.json
Server endpoints: /audit/forward/manifest (GET signed), /audit/forward/ack (POST ack window advance), /audit/forward/part-callback (POST part upload result)
CMEK handshake: use sealed-envelope pattern. Implement reference code in audit-crypto module and wire KMS integrations via adapters (aws-kms, gcp-kms, hsm-adapter).
Resumable uploads: rely on cloud provider multipart semantics; for on-prem agent use chunked checksums with explicit part sequence numbers recorded in manifest.
Backpressure: token-bucket per-tenant plus explicit ack window; window management persisted to tenant metadata with optimistic concurrency control.
Operator controls: console flags to set max-inflight-batches, preferred-upload-strategy (push/pull/delegated), retention overrides for forwarded sinks.

Observability: add metrics to Prometheus exporter: audit_forward_inflight_batches, audit_forward_upload_success_total, audit_forward_manifest_verification_failures_total, audit_forward_avg_delivery_latency_ms.
Compatibility: include a thin compatibility layer to translate existing legacy manifests into v1 for pilot customers (migration adaptor).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy manifest endpoint and push path to internal staging; test with synthetic tenant and minio on a private cluster (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable delegated and pull modes for 2 pilot customers; run a 7-day soak including simulated network interruptions and key rotations (3 weeks).
Phase 3 (soft launch): Expose to all Private/VPC customers behind feature flag; monitor metrics and disable-by-tenant if issues (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (GA): Promote feature flag by default with supporting docs and migration playbook (1 week).
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest serialization/deserialization and signature verification (coverage > 90%).
Integration tests for push/delegated/pull flows against mock S3/GCS/Azure and an on-prem reference agent; run in CI on every commit to main branch.
Fault-injection tests: simulate mid-upload connection loss and verify resumable completion and idempotency semantics.
Load test: synthetic workload targetting 500 rps with 10 tenants in staging; measure memory and latency targets recorded in acceptance criteria.
Security tests: pen-test the CMEK handshake flow and ensure no plaintext key exposure in logs or persisted stores.
